prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a production background atlas for a grand creation-myth game. THREE separate TALL PORTRAIT paintings, equal-width columns side by side, no gaps or frames, each column approximately 1:2.16 width-to-height; total canvas approximately 3:2.16. Reference image is a STYLE reference only: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink, deep lapis and jade, burnt ochre rock, coral accents and warm ivory light. These are full rectangular landscape paintings, NOT circular icons. The three scenes must preserve EXACTLY THE SAME geography and camera: an immense hook-shaped ochre headland at upper left, a single broad dark wave-cut cave at its foot above a small teal tidal inlet, distant serrated mountains across the upper right, one pale moon with a pair of unequal adjacent craters above. The cave has a dry upper rock shelf safely ABOVE the water, with its entrance clearly open. Vast scale, no tiny settlement, no houses, no divine person. Scene landmarks occupy the UPPER 43 percent of EACH portrait panel. The LOWER 57 percent is spacious, softly painted pale blue-grey and warm sand foreground with sparse broad flowing strokes, deliberately low contrast and calm, with no focal objects: this is the actual painted working area for game tokens. It must still feel like atmosphere and tidal foreground, not a blank UI panel, no overlays, no horizontal border. LEFT PANEL: primordial bare coastline after a sea cave has formed but BEFORE land vegetation or land animals. Bare ochre rocks, pale sea, serene immense sky; absolutely no plants, trees, animals or people. CENTER PANEL: the same headland and cave seen at the age of great fern forests. Tall frond-crowned trees mantle the distant high ground; two tiny long-necked sauropod-like herbivores browse on the ridge, ROUND broad feet, emphasizing landscape scale. NO flowers, fruit, grass meadow or buildings. Keep the low foreground calm. RIGHT PANEL: the same coast and former fern forest after a planetary impact winter. Sky muted ochre-grey, diffuse weak daylight, broken fern-tree trunks and empty black branches on the ridge, no living giant browsers or giant bodies; life has suffered and a lineage is lost. The sea and recognizable dry cave remain. Keep the lower working area a readable medium-light grey blue, not black. No flaming meteor, no ongoing explosion, no text, labels, letters, numbers, ornamental borders, circles or watermark. Match coastline outlines, cave opening and mountain silhouette across all three panels. Original painterly world, geographically plausible, atmospheric rather than photorealistic.
